subject: Urgent: BlueHarbor production API path anomaly / 5xx + latency spike
content:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@blueharbor.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@blueharbor.com>, BlueHarbor SRE oncall <oncall+blueharbor@sre.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 22:13:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production spike — 5xx + high latency from US-WEST clients

Marissa / Ben,

We're seeing a sustained 5xx spike and p99 latency jump across our US-WEST deployment starting ~21:50 PDT. End users are reporting timeouts and elevated token-generation latencies with Redwood models (hosted). Attached are a sample of request/response traces and a short set of app logs.

We suspect something in the network path — our infra team is seeing a flurry of route churn on the peering session to Redwood's us-west peering. Can you confirm whether anything changed on your side (peering, proxy pools, DNS/TLS)? This is impacting checkout flows.

Alex
Lead SRE, BlueHarbor Health
+1 415 555 0192

Subject: Re: Production spike — 5xx + high latency from US-WEST clients

Thanks Alex — seeing the alerts on our side as well. Ben and Rishi, I’m looping you in for triage.

Initial notes:
- Impact: multiple customer endpoints in us-west (our telemetry shows 5xx rate from ~2% -> 18% for BlueHarbor traffic, p99 latency up from ~180ms -> ~1.7s).
- Preliminary correlation: surge in proxy 503s + NAT exhaustion traces around the same time window.
- External hint from BlueHarbor: peering route churn observed.

Ben — can you confirm whether any peering rolls, firewall policy deploys, or DNS changes coincided with this window? If we confirm a peering flap on our edge, we should trigger route failover to alternate POPs and scrub the proxy pool.

I'll stand up a quick SEV channel and schedule a call if we need exec attention.

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 00:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production spike — BlueHarbor (triage notes)

Quick triage update — I pulled edge metrics and packet traces for the 21:45–22:05 window:
- Observed increased TCP retransmits between our us-west-2 peering fabric and BlueHarbor ASN; BGP keepalive resets from a transit provider were visible ~21:48.
- Our DNS fronting (short-lived A record rotation for proxy buckets) shows an abnormal TTL refresh behavior starting 21:45 — several clients continued to resolve to an older proxy pool which appears to have exhausted ephemeral ports.
- Proxy logs show a cluster of 503/504s when the old proxy pool hit max concurrent connections.

Attachments: trace-route-output-0917.png (traceroute showing asymmetric path), sample proxy logs in Drive.

Immediate recommended actions:
1) Force-route failover to us-west fallback POP (pop-id: rw-usw-fallback-3) for BlueHarbor traffic.
2) Increase ephemeral port pool and rotate proxy bucket for affected model route.
3) Coordinate with BlueHarbor to confirm they flush DNS caches / reduce client TTL for rapid cutover.

I can enact 1+2 immediately with a short maintenance window (~5 minutes); need BlueHarbor sign-off to proceed with cross-account route override.

-ben
Ben Carter
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Production spike — BlueHarbor (triage notes)

Thanks Ben — that aligns with what we saw on our side. Transit provider reports intermittent BGP flap in us-west for a single exchange and our edge team saw cached DNS entries pointing at the older proxy bucket.

Authorize route failover and increased ephemeral ports. We'll flush caches on our CDN/edge and open a ticket with transit.

Please proceed and keep this thread updated; we will standby for confirmation.

Alex

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Production spike — proposed action + exec note

Team — moving to action. Ben please execute the failover now. Olga, please prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) we can share with BlueHarbor leadership covering: timeline, root cause hypothesis (BGP transit flap + DNS cache + proxy ephemeral port exhaustion), mitigation steps taken, and proposed customer credits if SLA breach is confirmed.

Marissa — FYI this is likely to warrant exec attention given payment/checkout impact and potential SLA terms. I'm drafting an executive brief to surface to GTM and the Legal/Sales Ops teams; we should include: a summary of impact, mitigation steps, current ETA to restore (T+15m), and a proposal for a one-time credit + a follow-up joint review once we have full postmortem.

I'll join the call.

-rishi

Subject: Re: Production spike — MAP and immediate asks

Adding the MAP draft and a short checklist. I uploaded the doc and a few log extracts to Drive. High level MAP items:
- Immediate: forced POP failover (rw-usw-fallback-3), expand proxy ephemeral ports, rotate proxy bucket. Owner: Ben. ETA: 10 minutes.
- Short term (2–4 hours): BGP session stabilization with transit provider; coordinate DNS TTL shorten on BlueHarbor side; run flow tests across POPs. Owner: BlueHarbor + Redwood NRE.
- Postmortem: joint RCA within 72 hours, include packet captures, BGP telemetry, and proxy capacity graphs.
- Customer remediation: propose one week of service credits for impacted windows; to be finalized by Sales Ops.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-BlueHarbor.docx (document), log excerpts in Drive.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@blueharbor.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@blueharbor.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Production spike — BlueHarbor (status + exec ask)

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick approval earlier. Summary and current state:
- What happened: transient BGP flap at a transit exchange caused asymmetric routing; combined with stale DNS entries our traffic hit an older proxy cluster that exhausted ephemeral ports, producing elevated 5xx and p99 latency.
- What we did: forced POP failover at 00:40 PDT, increased ephemeral port pool, rotated proxy buckets, and requested BlueHarbor to flush CDN/edge caches. Visible customer errors decreased to baseline by ~01:05 PDT.
- Impact: approx. 18 minutes of elevated 5xx and degraded latency for a subset of US-WEST traffic. Customer reported checkout failures during that window (BlueHarbor internal error rate spike).
- Next steps: joint RCA and postmortem (72-hour target), confirm transit provider mitigations, and finalize customer credits.

Exec ask: Rishi and I recommend a short exec sync at 10:00 PDT to align on the credit proposal and customer comms (we'd like BlueHarbor leadership to join). Please reply with availability.

I'll put the MAP and the logs in the shared Drive link and open JIRA BH-4312 for postmortem actions.

Thanks again for the partnership — we'll follow up with the detailed RCA.

Marissa Cole
